claude.sample_unit: exercise plans (3 fictional patients x 3 prompts)

links.outcome: Safety of AI exercise plans vs ADA/ACSM guidelines, including contraindications and medical check-up advice
links.effect: Most common safety gap was missing advice for medical check-up (rated low in 8 of 9 plans); high-intensity training recommended for a patient with proliferative retinopathy; safety instructions incomplete.
links.quote: High-intensity training was recommended for Patient 3 with proliferative retinopathy.

links.outcome: Effect of prompt detail on plan quality and safety ratings across three prompts
links.effect: Safety ratings by prompt: Prompt 1 4L/3M/2S, Prompt 2 2L/2M/5S, Prompt 3 3L/2M/4S; more detailed prompts gave minimal safety improvement, and quality improved in some training criteria.
links.quote: Using more detailed prompts (Prompts 2 and 3) generally resulted in minimal quality improvement ( Figure 1 , Prompt 1: 4× L, 3× M, 2× S, Prompt 2: 2× L, 2× M, 5× S, Prompt 3: 3× L, 2× M, 4× S)

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering with detailed guideline-referencing prompts to improve LLM exercise plan quality
Professional coach review of LLM-generated exercise plans before patient use

links.effect: Safety ratings varied by prompt: Prompt 1 4×L/3×M/2×S; Prompt 2 2×L/2×M/5×S; Prompt 3 3×L/2×M/4×S.
links.quote: Using more detailed prompts (Prompts 2 and 3) generally resulted in minimal quality improvement ( Figure 1 , Prompt 1: 4× L, 3× M, 2× S, Prompt 2: 2× L, 2× M, 5× S, Prompt 3: 3× L, 2× M, 4× S), primarily in terms of tailoring the plans for individuals with secondary complications by avoiding conflicts between training and potential contraindications and providing additional safety instructions.

links.effect: ChatGPT recommended high-intensity training for a patient with proliferative retinopathy; another deficit was no balance exercises for older Patient 3.
links.quote: High-intensity training was recommended for Patient 3 with proliferative retinopathy.

links.effect: Medical-checkup advice was low in 8/9 plans; contraindication safety was low in 1/9 and moderate in 1/9; added safety instructions were moderate in 6/9.
links.quote: Several plans exhibited considerable safety gaps: The most common safety concern across all exercise plans was that users were not made aware of the need for a medical check-up prior to starting the training program, especially in cases of secondary conditions necessitating such a check-up (Patients 2 and 3) or when high-intensity workouts were recommended for sedentary patients [ 1 ].

links.effect: Across nine plans for three T2DM profiles, authors concluded the plans were not fully safe, especially for secondary diseases/complications.
links.quote: Our results imply that ChatGPT-4o-generated exercise plans are not (yet) fully safe for patients with T2DM, especially not for those with secondary diseases/complications.

unlisted_practices: Use more detailed prompts or prompt engineering that request guidelines, contraindications, goals, intensity, and preferences to improve ChatGPT-generated exercise plans.

links.outcome: Missed contraindications in generated exercise plans
links.effect: Contraindications were generally considered (7 plans strong), but high-intensity training was recommended for a patient with proliferative retinopathy (1 moderate, 1 low out of 9 plans).
links.quote: Potential contraindications were generally taken into consideration, with only a few exceptions: High-intensity training was recommended for Patient 3 with proliferative retinopathy.

unlisted_practices: Detailed prompting and prompt engineering incorporating clinical guidelines and contraindications
